## Scope and source notation

This audit uses only the supplied selected records, not the entire archive. Archive: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/work/scene_archive/bundles/r1--scene_rsi_pilot.tar.gz`. Below, **C1** and **C2** abbreviate member directories `experiments/scene_rsi_pilot/candidates/r1/scene_rsi_pilot/C1/` and `.../C2/`; **results** abbreviates `experiments/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/scene_rsi_pilot/`. Citations identify exact keys within the supplied member ranges.

## Detection and diagnosis

The initial teacher plan detected a **metric disagreement**, not its visual cause, for `commons_109923183` / `arm gold-1`; camera framing and object scale were hypotheses, with code location unknown (C1 `meta_execution.json` [0,2045), `plan.diagnoses`). Two controlled renders completed: focal length 51→56.1 changed overall 0.390749→0.387274; scaling the selected group by 1.1 changed it to 0.390894 with camera fixed and non-targets preserved. The target was a lexicographically selected group, not necessarily the whole object. These are sensitivity observations, not proof of camera error or 3D accuracy (C1 `diagnostic_observations.json` [0,4076), `probes[].result`, `visual_metrics`, `baseline_visual_metrics`).

Technical failure is distinct from visual quality. The later executed meta plan reports failed steps 1 and 3 for that scene, but their stderr fields are empty (C2 `meta_execution.json` [0,20132), `plan.diagnoses[0]`). C1’s proposal separately attributes earlier failures to fillet radius and world initialization; C2’s proposal reports two timeouts and no visual result for the camera revision. Those are proposal diagnoses, not independently detailed execution traces in the supplied records. C2 explicitly says the cross-scene mesh-count comparison does not establish timeout cause (C1 and C2 `proposal_result.json`, respectively [0,32641) and [0,15427), `diagnosis`).

## Proposed changes and observed mechanism

C1 proposed reusable H/policy and M changes: a same-role pre-execution review, build-failure handling, successful-render selection, and dependency-aware probe/regression planning. Its `policy.py` implements those branches; C1 `meta_execution.json` says the **initial** meta plan was actually used before proposal. C2 `meta_execution.json` identifies C1’s `meta.py` as its source and says that plan was actually used before the C2 proposal. This establishes meta-planning execution, not that every student-policy branch ran. C2 proposed inline rather than separate review, execution-time accounting and fallback selection; its proposal says M was unchanged (C1 `policy.py` [0,6998); C1 `meta_execution.json` `source`, `actually_used_for_proposal`; C2 `meta_execution.json` `source`, `actually_used_for_proposal`; C2 `proposal_result.json` `rationale`, `M_changed`).

The shared instructions address multiple-object inventory, semantic owners and unique slots; copying shared materials for local edits; keeping attached parts and relative transforms together; and separating object pose/scale from camera and appearance. C2 adds light/world versus local-material distinctions and leaves runner render settings fixed. These are safeguards and hypotheses, not demonstrated texture fidelity, correct pose, illumination, or physical contact (C1 `proposal_result.json` [0,32641), `files` entries `system.txt` and `meta.py`; C2 `policy.py` [0,12776), `PROCEDURE`).

## Tests and acceptance limits

C2’s diagnostics report prescribed Blender material replacement and group movement for C1’s `apron_-1` and `architecture`: target success, non-target preservation and relative-transform checks passed, with three renders completed each. These are actual recorded test operations, not student text edits. The selected groups are only a subset: projected structure shows 64 of 2,490 and 64 of 466 rows, respectively. No observed shared-material peers in those projections cannot certify omitted dependencies; AABBs cannot establish contact. Completeness and support/collision truth remain null (C2 `diagnostic_observations.json` [0,12942), `initial_diagnoses` for both targets, especially `dependencies.coverage`, `probe_result.material`, `probe_result.move`).

The functional rule treats an expected absent composite as failure, not N/A. C1 selection `commons_133800864` has `structure_pass: false` and `functional_pass: false`; C2’s two selection summaries pass, as do its four supplied test summaries. These results substantiate selected-target operability, not whole-scene quality or coverage (results `C1/selection/commons_133800864/functional/summary.json`; `C2/selection/{commons_133800864,commons_138420790}/functional/summary.json`; `C2/test/{commons_155212263,commons_16007442,commons_163096530,commons_199974832}/functional/summary.json`, exact `*_pass`, `interpretation` and null truth keys).

Both proposal revalidations record `status: accepted`, but also `newly_eligible: false`; acceptance of the candidate record must not be conflated with demonstrated visual improvement. The supplied records do not specify a complete candidate-selection threshold or establish one from scores. Neither proposal claims independent validation of improvement (C1 and C2 `proposal_result.json`, `status`, `scope`, `revalidation`).
